checklist.step: Open a market-entry licensing case from the approved business plan
actions: Take the signed market-entry approval from the Chief Underwriting Officer and record on a new licensing case: writing company legal name, NAIC company code, FEIN, target state, target Annual Statement lines, target first-write date.
Ask the Insurance Product Manager which products will be sold in the state and attach the product list, because the products drive the lines of authority requested.
Set the case type to Expansion (state already admitted for other lines) or New Admission (company not admitted in the state at all).
Name the case <company NAIC code>-<state>-<target write date> and open the evidence folder that every later artifact is filed into.
checklist.done: the licensing case carries company, NAIC code, state, requested lines and target first-write date, with the approved market-entry memo attached.

checklist.step: Read the current authority register entry for that company and state
actions: Open the authority register and filter to the writing company and the target state.
Read the record fields: CoA number, effective date, continuation date, authorised kinds of insurance, and any restriction or stipulation the DOI attached at admission.
Compare the authorised kinds of insurance to the lines the product list needs and mark each requested line COVERED, NOT COVERED or UNCLEAR.
Hand the NOT COVERED and UNCLEAR lines to the Regulatory Affairs Manager as the scope of the UCAA request.
checklist.done: each requested line is marked covered, not covered or unclear against the register, and the gap list is handed over.

checklist.step: Verify the live certificate against the regulator's own record, not the internal register
actions: In NAIC iSite+ open Company Information Search and pull the company by NAIC code, then open the State Licenses / Lines of Business panel for the target state.
Cross-check the same company on the state DOI's own company lookup (for Alaska, the Division of Insurance company search) because iSite+ lags state action by days.
Confirm status reads Active/Admitted and the licence has not been suspended, restricted or placed under a confidential order.
Export both screens to PDF named <state>-coa-verification-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and file them in the case folder — this is the evidence behind the covered/not-covered call.
Raise any disagreement between iSite+, the DOI record and the internal register to the Regulatory Affairs Manager the same day.
checklist.done: a dated capture of the NAIC and state DOI licence records exists and agrees with the internal authority register.

checklist.step: Map each product to the state's statutory kinds of insurance and Annual Statement line codes
actions: Open the target state's insurance code section that enumerates kinds of insurance (representative: Alaska Stat. §§ 21.12.010–21.12.110) and list the exact statutory labels.

Map each product's coverage to one statutory kind and to the Annual Statement line code used on the Statutory Page 14 exhibit (e.g. 5.1 Commercial Multiple Peril, 19.2 Other Private Passenger Auto Liability).
Flag hybrid products whose coverage spans two kinds — those need both lines on the certificate before a single policy can be bound.
Send the mapping to the Chief Underwriting Officer for written confirmation that no product exceeds the mapped lines, and file the reply.
checklist.done: every product has a named statutory kind of insurance, an Annual Statement line code and written CUO confirmation of scope.

checklist.step: Pull the state's UCAA Expansion requirements checklist for the filing year
actions: Open the NAIC UCAA page and download the current-year Expansion Application form set and the target state's State Specific Requirements checklist.
Read the state page for whether it accepts the Expansion Application at all, the filing fee amount, the payment method (NAIC OPTins vs state check) and the reviewer contact.

List every required exhibit on the case sheet: Uniform Consent to Service of Process, Certificate of Compliance and Certificate of Deposit from the domiciliary state, audited and statutory financials, plan of operation, biographical affidavits, holding company registration.
Save the dated checklist PDF into the case folder as the authority for what the package must contain.
checklist.done: the current-year state-specific UCAA checklist is filed and every required exhibit is listed with an owner.

checklist.step: Obtain the domiciliary Certificate of Compliance and Certificate of Deposit
actions: Request from the domiciliary regulator (representative: Iowa Insurance Division) a Certificate of Compliance naming the company and every line it is authorised to write at home, and a Certificate of Deposit listing securities on deposit.
Check the certificates are dated within the freshness window the target state's checklist states (commonly 60 days) — an older certificate will be rejected at intake.
Confirm the lines named on the Certificate of Compliance are a superset of the lines being requested in the target state; a line not written at home cannot usually be expanded into.
File both originals in the case folder and log their issue dates so re-ordering can be triggered if review runs long.
checklist.done: in-date Certificates of Compliance and Deposit are on file and their line lists cover every requested line.

checklist.step: Test capital, surplus and the state's deposit condition before filing
actions: Read the target state's minimum paid-in capital and minimum surplus requirement for the specific kinds of insurance requested — the amount rises with each additional line.
Pull capital and surplus from the most recent filed Annual Statement (Liabilities, Surplus and Other Funds page) and the latest quarterly, and compute headroom against the state minimum.
Compute the RBC ratio from the filed RBC report and confirm it sits above the Company Action Level, since admission review will look at it.
Where a special deposit is required for the state, instruct the Treasury Manager to post the security and obtain the custodian receipt.
Record the tested figures, the source statement date and the pass/fail conclusion on the case sheet.
checklist.done: capital, surplus, RBC and any state deposit are computed against the state minimum with the source statement cited.

checklist.step: Assemble the biographical affidavits and third-party verifications
actions: Identify every officer and director the state's checklist requires an affidavit for, plus any person owning 10% or more of the company.
Issue the current NAIC Biographical Affidavit (Form 11) to each individual and collect it notarised and signed within the last 12 months.
Order the third-party background verification report from the NAIC-accepted vendor for each affidavit and check the report resolves every name, address and employment gap disclosed.
Compare each affidavit to the board minute book so titles, appointment dates and directorships agree with the corporate record.
File affidavits and verification reports in the case folder under restricted access and note the completion date.
checklist.done: every required officer and director has a notarised, in-date affidavit with a matching third-party verification report on file.

checklist.step: Prepare the plan of operation and the corporate exhibits
actions: Write the plan of operation for the state: products to be sold, distribution channel, three-year premium projections by line, reinsurance program summary and claims-handling arrangements.
Attach the certified articles of incorporation and bylaws, the current corporate structure chart and the Form B holding company registration statement.
Execute the Uniform Consent to Service of Process naming the state's Commissioner or Director and, where the state requires it, appoint a registered agent in the state.
Have Regulatory Counsel review the plan of operation and the consent form for consistency with the requested lines before submission.
checklist.done: the plan of operation, corporate exhibits and executed consent to service of process are counsel-reviewed and filing-ready.

checklist.step: Submit the UCAA Expansion package and pay the admission fee
actions: Assemble the package in the exact tab order the state's checklist prescribes and complete the Expansion Application cover form with NAIC code, FEIN, lines requested and effective date sought.
Submit by the channel the state names — electronic submission to the DOI licensing mailbox or the state portal — and pay the admission fee through NAIC OPTins where the state accepts it.
Record the submission date, the confirmation or transaction number and the assigned DOI reviewer on the case sheet.
Diarise the state's stated review period and set a follow-up to the reviewer if nothing is heard by two-thirds of it.
checklist.done: the package is submitted, the fee is paid and the submission date, confirmation number and reviewer are recorded.

checklist.step: Work every DOI deficiency letter to closure
actions: Log each deficiency item from the DOI letter as its own row with the item, the responder role and a due date inside the response window the letter states.
Route financial items to the Statutory Reporting Manager, corporate items to the Corporate Secretary and legal items to Regulatory Counsel, with the letter attached.
Send one consolidated response per letter referencing the DOI's item numbering, and keep the transmittal email in the case folder.
Update the target first-write date whenever a deficiency cycle pushes the expected grant date, and tell the Insurance Product Manager the same day.
checklist.done: every deficiency item has a dated response filed with the DOI and the case shows a revised expected grant date.

checklist.step: Record the granted certificate in the authority register
actions: Open the granted certificate PDF and key into the register: CoA number, grant date, effective date, each authorised kind of insurance, continuation date and any stipulation.
Attach the certificate PDF and the grant letter to the register row and set the record status to Active.
Set the annual continuation reminder for the state's renewal date with T-120/T-60/T-30 alerts.
Have the Regulatory Affairs Manager verify the keyed lines character-for-character against the certificate before the row is published.
checklist.done: the register holds an Active row matching the certificate line for line, with the PDF attached and continuation alerts set.

checklist.step: Arm the quote and bind gate in the policy administration platform
actions: Open the writing-company availability configuration and enable the state and each newly authorised line with an effective date equal to the CoA effective date, never earlier.
Keep every unauthorised state/line combination hard-blocked at quote so an underwriter cannot override it into a bind.
Ask the Underwriting Director / Manager to run one test quote in the new state and one in an unauthorised line, and confirm the second is refused.
Attach the configuration change ticket and the two test results to the licensing case.
checklist.done: the new state/line quotes only from the CoA effective date and an unauthorised line is proven to be refused at quote.

checklist.step: Continue the certificate each year and prove the continuation conditions still hold
actions: Ahead of each state's renewal date, confirm the annual statement and any state-required continuation form were filed and the continuation fee paid through NAIC OPTins.
Re-test capital, surplus and the statutory deposit against the state's current minimum using the just-filed Annual Statement figures.
Confirm no examination finding, order or corrective plan restricts the certificate, by checking the state DOI record and the exam correspondence file.
Record the continuation confirmation and receipt against the register row and roll the continuation date forward one year.
checklist.done: each certificate shows a paid, confirmed continuation for the current year with capital and deposit re-tested against the current minimum.

checklist.step: File the licensing case evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the case folder — application, checklist, certificates of compliance and deposit, affidavits, deficiency correspondence, granted certificate, continuation receipts — into the repository under Licensing / CoA / <state> / <company>.
Apply the 10-years-from-withdrawal retention label so the record survives a later voluntary withdrawal from the state.
Confirm the repository index makes the record searchable by NAIC company code, state and CoA number.
Link the repository record back to the authority register row so an examiner request resolves in one hop.
checklist.done: the case is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by NAIC code, state and CoA number from the register row.

testing.step: Build the population of policies bound in the quarter by state and line
actions: Extract every new-business and renewal policy with a bind date in the quarter, with writing company NAIC code, risk state, Annual Statement line code and effective date.
Add endorsements that added a new coverage line mid-term, because those can push a policy outside the certificate after issue.
Reconcile the extract premium total to the quarter's Page 14 statutory premium by state and resolve any difference before sampling.
Have the extractor sign the population as complete and date the extract.
testing.done: the bound-policy population reconciles to statutory premium by state and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile every bound state/line to an active certificate at the bind date
actions: Join each population row to the authority register on company + state + Annual Statement line code.
Check the register row's status was Active and its effective date was on or before the bind date, and that no suspension covered that date.
List unmatched rows, rows bound before the CoA effective date and rows bound in a line not on the certificate as automatic exceptions.
Quantify each exception in policy count and written premium for the escalation memo.
testing.done: every bound row matches an active, in-date certificate line or is listed as a quantified exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of states entered or lines added during the quarter and 100% of certificates whose continuation fell in the quarter.
Take 25 further policy rows by seeded random selection across the remaining states, minimum 40 rows in total.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
Note in the workpaper which states are represented so coverage gaps across the 51 jurisdictions are visible.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all new entries and continuations, and its state coverage is stated.

testing.step: Re-perform the certificate verification in the regulator's system
actions: For each sampled state, look the company up independently in NAIC iSite+ Company Information Search and on the state DOI company lookup, without reading the internal register first.
Read the licence status, effective date and authorised kinds of insurance, then compare to the register row.
Treat any difference as an exception, including a register line that is broader than the certificate wording.
Capture both lookup screens into the workpaper with the retrieval date.
testing.done: each sampled state has an independent regulator-source verification captured and compared to the register.

testing.step: Re-test the product-to-line mapping behind the sampled binds
actions: For each sampled policy read the issued coverage forms and decide independently which statutory kind of insurance the coverage falls under.
Compare that to the Annual Statement line code the policy was coded to and to the kinds named on the certificate.
Flag hybrid policies where one coverage part sits outside the certificate even though the main line is authorised.
Record the re-performed mapping and the statute section relied on for each sampled policy.
testing.done: every sampled policy has an independently re-performed line mapping tied to a cited statutory kind of insurance.

testing.step: Recompute the capital, surplus and deposit conditions for sampled states
actions: Read the current minimum paid-in capital and surplus for the sampled state and the specific lines held.
Recompute headroom from the filed Annual Statement capital and surplus figures as at the continuation date, not today.
Confirm the statutory deposit securities on the custodian statement still meet the state's required amount and eligible-asset rules.
Any state below the minimum at any point in the quarter is a reportable condition, not a documentation exception.
testing.done: capital, surplus and deposit are recomputed against the state minimum at the continuation date for every sampled state.

testing.step: Trace each continuation to a paid fee and a confirmed renewal
actions: For every continuation due in the quarter, obtain the NAIC OPTins transaction record or the state receipt and read the payment date against the state's renewal date.
Confirm any state-required continuation form or annual certification was filed and acknowledged.
Check the state DOI record still shows the certificate Active after the renewal date.
Late or unpaid continuations are exceptions regardless of whether the state ultimately renewed.
testing.done: every continuation traces to a dated payment, a filed form and an Active post-renewal regulator record.

testing.step: Prove the quote and bind gate actually blocks unauthorised business
actions: Pull the writing-company availability configuration and compare its enabled state/line matrix line by line to the authority register.
Have the Policy Admin Ops Lead run a controlled quote in a state/line combination that is not on any certificate and capture the refusal.
Review the override and exception log for the quarter for any manual unlock of a blocked state or line and read the approver.
Any configuration row enabled ahead of a CoA effective date is an exception even if nothing was bound under it.
testing.done: the system matrix agrees with the register, the block is demonstrated, and every override is identified and owned.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with policy number, state, line, premium and what condition was breached.
Assign a root cause — configuration enabled early, register keyed wider than the certificate, continuation missed, product mapped to the wrong line — and an owner.
For any unauthorised writing, open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel covering rescission, reinsurance of the risk and DOI notification.
Set remediation dates and carry every open item into the next quarter as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where writing was unauthorised, a counsel-led self-report decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate in policies and premium and compare it to the zero-tolerance threshold.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who performed no CoA verification or register maintenance in the period, sign the workpaper.
Report results, unauthorised-writing breaches and self-reports to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the exception rate, the conclusion and the committee reporting date, and is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Take in the contracting request and open the producer record
actions: Receive the contracting request from the Agency Relations Manager with producer legal name, NPN, SSN or FEIN, resident state, the states to be appointed and the products to be sold.
Create the producer record with status 'Pending — unverified' so no downstream system can issue credentials against it.
Reject any request without an NPN — the NPN is the key every later verification is run on.
Attach the signed producer agreement or agency contract and record its execution date, because the appointment clock runs from it.
checklist.done: a Pending producer record exists with NPN, resident state, requested states, product list and a dated contract attached.

checklist.step: Pull the Producer Database report for the producer
actions: In NIPR Gateway open the Producer Database and run a PDB report by NPN, or by SSN/FEIN where the NPN is unknown.
Read the report's licence section for every requested state: licence number, licence class (producer, adjuster, business entity), status, original issue date and expiration date.
Read the report's Regulatory Actions and Appointments sections in full — a licence can be active while carrying an open administrative action.
Save the PDB PDF to the producer record named <NPN>-pdb-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf; a report older than 30 days may not be relied on at appointment.
checklist.done: a dated PDB report is attached to the producer record covering every requested state.

checklist.step: Match lines of authority to the products the producer will actually sell
actions: List the products from the contracting request and translate each to the line of authority the state uses — Life, Accident & Health, Property, Casualty, Personal Lines, Variable Contracts, Surplus Lines.
Compare that list against the lines of authority shown on the PDB for each state and mark each product AUTHORISED or NOT AUTHORISED.
Where the producer will sell variable annuities or variable life, additionally confirm the FINRA registration and broker-dealer affiliation with the Annuity Suitability Analyst.
Record on the producer record which products are releasable and which are blocked pending an additional line of authority.
checklist.done: every product is marked authorised or blocked against the producer's actual lines of authority in that state.

checklist.step: Test the resident versus non-resident position for each requested state
actions: Identify the producer's resident state from the PDB and confirm the resident licence is active — a lapsed resident licence collapses every non-resident licence built on it.
For each other requested state, confirm a non-resident licence exists with the matching lines of authority.
Where a non-resident licence is missing, submit the non-resident application through NIPR Gateway ▸ Non-Resident Licensing for that state, pay the state fee and record the transaction number.
Diarise the state's typical turnaround and re-pull the PDB to confirm issuance before any solicitation is permitted.
checklist.done: the resident licence is confirmed active and every requested state has an issued non-resident licence or a tracked pending application.

checklist.step: Verify the agency entity licence and its designated responsible licensee
actions: Where the counterparty is a firm, run the PDB by FEIN and confirm the business entity licence is active in each state with the required lines.
Identify the designated responsible licensed producer named on the entity licence and confirm that individual's own licence is active in the same state.
Check the entity's assumed or DBA name on the licence matches the name on the agency contract and the name that will appear on solicitation material.
Ask the Agency Relations Manager for the sub-producer roster the agency intends to place business through and verify each one before the agency is released.
checklist.done: the entity licence, its designated responsible licensee and the named sub-producer roster are all verified active.

checklist.step: Read the regulatory-action and background flags before eligibility is granted
actions: Open the PDB Regulatory Actions section and list every action with state, date, disposition and any fine or suspension.
Pull the underlying state order from the issuing DOI's enforcement page for any action less than five years old.
Refer any action involving dishonesty, breach of trust or misappropriation of premium to the 18 U.S.C. § 1033 screening step before contracting proceeds.
Record the eligibility decision, the reviewer and the date on the producer record — never leave a flagged producer with a silent approval.
checklist.done: every regulatory action is listed, sourced to the issuing order where recent, and a dated eligibility decision is recorded.

checklist.step: Confirm the company itself is authorised in the state before appointing anyone into it
actions: Open the authority register and confirm the writing company holds an active certificate of authority in the state for the lines the producer will sell.
Where the certificate does not cover a line, block that line on the producer record — a licensed producer cannot cure an unauthorised insurer.
Record the CoA number and the line codes relied on against the producer record so the two registers are traceably linked.
Escalate any mismatch to the Regulatory Affairs Manager the same day.
checklist.done: each releasable producer state/line is backed by an active company certificate of authority recorded on the producer record.

checklist.step: Collect the contracting packet and background authorisations
actions: Issue the contracting packet for signature: producer agreement, commission schedule, background and credit check authorisation, W-9, EFT authorisation and errors-and-omissions certificate.
Check the E&O certificate names the producer or agency, is in force at the contract date and meets the company's minimum limit and retention.
Confirm the W-9 name and TIN match the licence name on the PDB, because a mismatch will break both appointment and commission reporting.
File the completed packet against the producer record and record the completion date.
checklist.done: a complete, signed contracting packet with an in-force E&O certificate and a name/TIN match to the PDB is on file.

checklist.step: Set the appointment eligibility flag and hand the record to Licensing Ops
actions: Move the producer record from 'Pending — unverified' to 'Eligible for appointment' only when licence, lines, entity, CoA and packet checks all read pass.
Write the verification summary onto the record: PDB pull date, licence numbers per state, lines released, lines blocked, reviewer and date.
Hand the record to Licensing Ops with the contract execution date so the statutory appointment window is calculated from the right date.
Leave a blocked-line list visible on the record so nobody quietly releases a product later without re-verification.
checklist.done: the record reads Eligible with a dated verification summary and a visible blocked-line list, and Licensing Ops has the contract date.

checklist.step: Release quoting credentials only after the eligibility flag is set
actions: Provision the portal account only for producers reading 'Eligible for appointment' and only for the states and lines released on the record.
Configure the portal entitlements so a blocked line does not render as a quotable product for that producer.
Send the welcome pack that states plainly the producer may not solicit in a state until the licence and appointment are confirmed active.
Log the provisioning date and the entitlement set against the producer record.
checklist.done: portal entitlements exist only for released state/line combinations and the provisioning date is logged.

checklist.step: Re-verify at every material change to the relationship
actions: Re-pull the PDB whenever the producer requests a new state, a new product line, or changes legal name, resident state or agency affiliation.
Subscribe the producer's NPN to NIPR alerts so licence lapses, cancellations and new regulatory actions arrive without being asked for.
On any lapse alert, set the producer to solicit-blocked in the producer management system and suspend portal entitlements the same business day.
Notify the Agency Relations Manager and the servicing underwriter so in-flight submissions are re-assigned rather than quietly bound.
checklist.done: every material change triggers a fresh PDB pull, and lapse alerts block solicitation and portal access the same day.

checklist.step: Run the daily automated roster-to-PDB check
actions: Submit the active producer roster to the NIPR licence-status service on a daily schedule keyed on NPN and state.
Compare the returned status and lines of authority to the producer management system record and write differences to an exception queue.
Work the queue the same day: expired, cancelled and suspended licences trigger an immediate solicit block.
Report the daily exception count and the ageing of unresolved items to the Producer Compliance Manager.
checklist.done: the daily check runs on the full roster and every returned difference is worked or blocked within the same business day.

checklist.step: Stop and remediate business found to have been solicited without a licence
actions: Pull every application and bound policy attributable to the producer between the licence lapse date and the block date.
Instruct the Commission Analyst to place commissions on those transactions in withholding pending the disposition decision.
Ask Regulatory Counsel whether the state requires notification and whether affected policies must be reassigned to a licensed producer of record.
Record the affected policy list, premium at risk and the disposition on the exception record.
checklist.done: affected policies and premium are quantified, commissions are withheld and a counsel-led disposition is recorded.

checklist.step: Report producer licensing status into distribution governance
actions: Publish a monthly dashboard showing eligible, pending, blocked and lapsed producer counts by state and channel.
Show ageing on pending verifications and on unresolved daily-check exceptions so bottlenecks are visible to the Head of Distribution.
Table the dashboard at the monthly distribution governance meeting with the top three root causes of blocks.
Record the meeting decisions and owners against the licensing case log.
checklist.done: a monthly dashboard with ageing and root causes is tabled at distribution governance with recorded decisions.

checklist.step: Retain the verification evidence for the producer relationship
actions: File the PDB reports, verification summaries, contracting packet and eligibility decisions under Licensing / Producer Verification / <NPN>.
Apply the 7-years-after-termination retention label so the record survives the producer leaving.
Confirm the record is retrievable by NPN, licence number and producer legal name.
Link the repository record to the producer management system record so an exam request resolves in one hop.
checklist.done: verification evidence is filed by NPN, retention-labelled and retrievable from the producer record.

testing.step: Build the population of producers and of producer-attributed business
actions: Extract every producer contracted, re-activated or newly released to a state in the quarter with NPN, states, lines and eligibility date.
Extract every application and bound policy in the quarter from the policy administration platform with writing producer NPN, risk state, line and transaction date.
Reconcile the distinct producer NPNs on the transaction extract to the producer roster and investigate any NPN transacting that is absent from the roster.
Sign and date the population as complete.
testing.done: both populations are extracted, the transacting NPNs reconcile to the roster, and the population is signed.

testing.step: Reconcile every transaction to an active licence on the transaction date
actions: Join each transaction to the PDB licence history for that NPN and state, matching on the transaction date rather than today's status.
Confirm the licence was active and carried the line of authority the product needed on that date.
List transactions with no licence, a lapsed licence or a missing line of authority as automatic exceptions with premium and commission attached.
Separate exceptions caused by a lapse from those caused by a line-of-authority gap, since the root causes differ.
testing.done: every transaction is matched to a date-effective active licence with the right line, or listed as a quantified exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of producers released to a new state in the quarter and 100% of producers with any regulatory action on the PDB.
Take 30 producers by seeded random selection across the remaining roster, stratified so no single state exceeds a fifth of the sample.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date so the sample is reproducible.
State in the workpaper how many of the 51 jurisdictions the sample touches.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all new releases and flagged producers, and its jurisdiction coverage is stated.

testing.step: Re-pull the PDB independently for each sampled producer
actions: Run a fresh PDB report by NPN in NIPR Gateway without reading the filed verification summary first.
Record licence number, class, status, issue and expiry date and lines of authority per state from your own pull.
Compare to the filed verification summary and treat any difference — including a line recorded that the PDB does not show — as an exception.
Attach both your pull and the filed report to the workpaper with retrieval dates.
testing.done: each sampled producer has an independently retrieved PDB compared line by line to the filed verification.

testing.step: Re-perform the line-of-authority match against products actually sold
actions: For each sampled producer, list the products they actually placed in the quarter from the policy extract, not the products requested at contracting.
Map each placed product to the state's line of authority independently and compare to the producer's held lines.
Flag every product sold outside a held line, including variable products sold without the variable contracts authority.
Record the re-performed mapping and the state taxonomy source used.
testing.done: every product actually placed is mapped to a held line of authority or logged as a sold-outside-authority exception.

testing.step: Test the pre-solicitation timing on the sample
actions: For each sampled producer take the earliest application or quote date in the state from the transaction extract.
Compare it to the licence issue date on the PDB and to the eligibility date on the producer record.
Any solicitation dated before the licence issue date is a breach; any dated before the internal eligibility date is a control failure.
Record both date comparisons and the day counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: earliest solicitation, licence issue and eligibility dates are compared with day counts for every sampled producer.

testing.step: Test entity licences and designated responsible licensees
actions: For sampled agencies run the PDB by FEIN and confirm the entity licence status and lines in each state where business was placed.
Confirm the named designated responsible licensee held an active individual licence throughout the quarter.
Trace at least three sub-producers per sampled agency to their own active licences for the business they wrote.
Flag any agency placing business through an unverified sub-producer.
testing.done: each sampled agency's entity licence, responsible licensee and traced sub-producers are verified active for the period.

testing.step: Test the portal entitlement gate against the eligibility record
actions: Extract the portal entitlement list by producer, state and product and compare it to the released state/line list on the producer record.
Identify any entitlement that exists for a blocked line or for a producer not reading Eligible.
Read the provisioning approval trail for each such entitlement and name the approver.
Confirm producers set to solicit-blocked during the quarter had entitlements suspended within one business day of the block.
testing.done: portal entitlements reconcile to released lines and every over-entitlement is identified with a named approver.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation
actions: Raise a tracker issue per exception with NPN, state, line, transaction dates, premium and commission at risk.
Assign a root cause — stale PDB, line mismatch, entitlement provisioned early, lapse alert not worked — and an owner.
For unlicensed solicitation, record the commission withholding decision and Regulatory Counsel's view on state notification and producer-of-record reassignment.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where unlicensed, a commission and notification decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate in producers and in premium and compare it to the zero-tolerance threshold.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who verified none of the sampled producers, sign the workpaper.
Report results and any unlicensed-solicitation breaches to the Compliance Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the exception rate, conclusion and committee reporting date and is filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Detect the appointment trigger and stamp the statutory clock start
actions: Run the daily trigger report that surfaces two events: a producer agreement executed in the last 24 hours, and the first application received from a producer in a state where no appointment exists.
Stamp the clock-start date on the producer-state row as the earlier of the contract execution date and the first application receipt date.
Pull the first-application date directly from the policy administration submission log rather than accepting the underwriter's word for it.
Set the due date by adding that state's statutory window to the clock-start date and put the row into the appointment queue.
checklist.done: every triggered producer-state row shows a sourced clock-start date and a state-specific due date in the queue.

checklist.step: Apply the per-state appointment window table
actions: Open the per-state window table and confirm the entry for the state: window length, whether the trigger is the contract or the first application, and whether the state is appointment-optional.
For appointment-optional or notification-only states, record the alternate treatment on the row so the queue does not chase a filing that is not required.
Re-validate any state entry not reviewed in the last 12 months against the state's current statute text before relying on it.
Date and initial the table entry used, so the due date can be defended later.
checklist.done: the row cites the state window entry used, its trigger basis and its last validation date.

checklist.step: Confirm licence and company authority still hold at the moment of appointment
actions: Re-pull the PDB for the NPN and confirm the licence is active in that state with the lines the appointment will cover — a PDB older than 30 days is not sufficient.
Confirm on the authority register that the writing company holds an active certificate of authority in that state for those lines.
Stop the transaction if either check fails and return the row to the Producer Compliance Manager rather than submitting and hoping.
Record both confirmations and their dates on the row.
checklist.done: a fresh PDB and an active company certificate are recorded against the row before submission.

checklist.step: Submit the appointment transaction in NIPR
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Appointments ▸ New Appointment, select the writing company NAIC code and the state, and enter the producer NPN.
Select the appointment types and lines the state offers and requested effective date, matching the lines to those on the licence.
Confirm the state appointment fee and submit, capturing the NIPR transaction id and submission timestamp.
Write the transaction id and timestamp back to the producer-state row and leave the row Open — submission is not completion.
checklist.done: the appointment is submitted with a captured NIPR transaction id and timestamp against the row.

checklist.step: Match the state confirmation back to the submission and close the row
actions: Pull the daily NIPR appointment response file and match each response to an open row on transaction id.
Read the state's returned status and appointment effective date; write the effective date onto the row.

Work rejections the same day — common causes are a lapsed licence, a line not held, an unpaid fee or a NAIC code mismatch — and resubmit inside the original statutory window, not from the rejection date.
Close the row only when a state effective date is recorded.
checklist.done: every submitted row carries a state effective date or an in-window resubmission, and no row closes without confirmation.

checklist.step: Release the producer to write in the state
actions: On confirmation, enable the state and lines in the producer's portal entitlements with an effective date equal to the state appointment effective date.
Notify the Agency Relations Manager and the servicing underwriter that the producer is appointed and from which date.
Where the state permitted business before appointment on the first-application trigger, confirm the appointment was filed within the window so that business is not retrospectively exposed.
Record the entitlement change ticket against the producer-state row.
checklist.done: portal entitlements match the confirmed appointment effective date and the change ticket is linked to the row.

checklist.step: Work the aged appointment queue every day
actions: Sort the open appointment queue by days remaining to the state due date and work the smallest first.
Escalate any row at day 10 of a 15-day window to the Producer Compliance Manager with the blocking reason named.
Record for any breached row the actual filing date, the day count over and the reason.
Report the queue ageing and the breach count to the Producer Compliance Manager daily.
checklist.done: the queue is worked daily, rows nearing the window are escalated and every breach records a day count and reason.

checklist.step: Detect the termination event and freeze the producer's ability to write
actions: Take the separation trigger from the Agency Relations Manager, the contract termination notice or the HR leaver feed and stamp the termination effective date on every affected producer-state row.
Suspend portal entitlements and quoting access the same day so no new business is written under a terminated appointment.
List every state where an active appointment exists for that producer, because each state requires its own filing.
Set the termination filing due date per state from the state window table.
checklist.done: every state with an active appointment is listed with its own due date, and writing access is suspended the same day.

checklist.step: Determine and document the reason for termination
actions: Classify the termination as not-for-cause or for-cause using the state's own reason codes, which cover conduct such as misappropriation of premium, fraud, forgery and violation of insurance law.
For a for-cause termination assemble the supporting file: investigation summary, dates, amounts, documents relied on and the internal decision record.
Have Regulatory Counsel review the for-cause narrative before it is transmitted, because the statement carries the statutory immunity only if made in good faith and without malice.
Record the classification, the reason code and the counsel review date on the row.
checklist.done: each termination has a state reason code, a supporting file where for-cause, and a counsel review date.

checklist.step: File the termination in NIPR within the state window
actions: In NIPR Gateway open Appointments ▸ Terminations, select the writing company and state and enter the NPN and termination effective date.
Select the state's termination reason code and, for cause, attach or transmit the narrative in the format the state accepts.
Submit and capture the NIPR transaction id and submission timestamp on the row.
Match the state response file back to the row and record the state's acknowledged termination date.
checklist.done: each terminated appointment has a submitted transaction, a captured id and an acknowledged state termination date.

checklist.step: Send the producer their statutory copy of the notice
actions: Generate the producer notice letter reproducing what was reported to the state, including the reason code where the state requires the producer to receive it.
Send it to the producer's address of record on the PDB within the state's producer-notice window (representatively 15 days from the state filing).
Use a trackable delivery method and file the dispatch proof and delivery record against the row.
Log any producer response or dispute and route it to Regulatory Counsel.
checklist.done: a dated producer notice with delivery proof is filed for every termination inside the producer-notice window.

checklist.step: Handle additional or corrected information the state must receive
actions: Where facts material to the termination reason emerge after filing, prepare a supplemental notice to the state within the state's supplemental window (commonly 30 days of discovery).
Have Regulatory Counsel clear the supplemental narrative on the same good-faith basis as the original.
File the supplement through the same NIPR termination channel and capture its transaction id.
Update the original row to reference the supplement so the record reads as one history.
checklist.done: post-filing material facts are supplemented to the state within the window and linked to the original row.

checklist.step: Reconcile appointment fee billing and state invoices
actions: Pull the NIPR fee statement for the month and match each charge to an appointment or termination transaction id on the register.
Identify charges with no matching register row and register rows with no charge, and resolve both before the month closes.
Check states that bill appointment renewals separately (annual or biennial invoices) have been paid, since an unpaid renewal cancels the appointment.
Hand the reconciliation to the Producer Compliance Manager with the unresolved list.
checklist.done: every NIPR and state appointment charge reconciles to a register row and unpaid renewals are identified.

checklist.step: Escalate and remediate window breaches
actions: Raise an issue for each filing made outside the state window with the state, NPN, trigger date, filing date and day count over.
Identify the business written in the gap and quantify premium and commission exposure with the Commission Analyst.
Assess with Regulatory Counsel whether the state assesses a late fee, requires a reinstatement transaction or expects a self-report.
Assign an owner and a remediation date and feed the root cause into the next procedure review.
checklist.done: every breach has a quantified gap, a counsel-assessed regulatory consequence, an owner and a remediation date.

checklist.step: Retain the appointment and termination record
actions: File per producer-state: trigger evidence, PDB pull, NIPR transaction ids, state confirmations, reason code file and producer notice with delivery proof.
Apply the 7-years-after-termination retention label.
Confirm the record is searchable by NPN, state, transaction id and termination effective date.
Link the repository record to the producer management system row.
checklist.done: the full appointment/termination history is filed, retention-labelled and searchable by NPN, state and transaction id.

testing.step: Build the population of appointment triggers and terminations in the quarter
actions: Extract every producer agreement executed in the quarter and every first application received from an unappointed producer, with NPN, state and date.
Extract every producer separation in the quarter with the termination effective date and every state where an appointment was active.
Reconcile the trigger extract against the policy administration first-submission log so triggers cannot be missed by relying on the contract log alone.
Sign and date the population as complete.
testing.done: trigger and termination populations are extracted, reconciled to submission data and signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the appointment register
actions: Match every trigger row to an appointment register row on NPN + state + company.
Match every separation row to a termination register row for each state where an appointment was active.
List unmatched triggers and unmatched terminations as automatic exceptions — an unfiled termination leaves an appointment live.
Quantify how many states each unmatched producer touched.
testing.done: every trigger and separation matches a register row or is listed as an unfiled exception with its state count.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of for-cause terminations and 100% of events in states with a window shorter than 15 days.
Take 40 further events by seeded random selection split evenly between appointments and terminations.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date for reproducibility.
State how many distinct jurisdictions the sample covers.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all for-cause terminations and short-window states, and its jurisdiction spread is stated.

testing.step: Recompute the statutory day count for each sampled event
actions: Read the state's window directly from the statute for the sampled state rather than from the internal window table.
Recompute due date = trigger date + statutory window, using the trigger the statute names (contract execution or first application) and the state's calendar-vs-business-day convention.
Compare the recomputed due date to the actual NIPR submission date and record days early or late.
Treat a wrong entry in the internal window table as a systemic exception affecting every event in that state.
testing.done: each sampled event has an independently recomputed due date and a days-early/late figure against the actual filing.

testing.step: Trace each sampled filing to the NIPR transaction and the state confirmation
actions: Look up the recorded NIPR transaction id in NIPR Gateway and confirm it exists for the right company NAIC code, state and NPN.
Read the state's returned status and effective date and compare to the register row.
Where a transaction was rejected and resubmitted, confirm the resubmission still landed inside the original statutory window.
Capture the transaction detail screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled filing traces to a real NIPR transaction with a state confirmation captured in the workpaper.

testing.step: Test for business written while unappointed
actions: For each sampled producer-state, pull policies bound between the trigger date and the state appointment effective date.
Determine whether the state permits writing on the first-application trigger before appointment confirmation, and where it does not, flag every such policy.
For terminated producers, pull policies bound after the termination effective date and flag any.
Quantify premium and commission on every flagged policy.
testing.done: business written outside an active appointment window is identified per sampled producer and quantified in premium and commission.

testing.step: Re-perform the for-cause termination support
actions: Read the state reason code reported and the underlying investigation file for each for-cause termination.
Confirm the reported reason is supported by dated evidence and matches the state's code definition, not a paraphrase.
Confirm the narrative was reviewed by counsel before transmission and that no material fact discovered later went unsupplemented.
Treat a for-cause code filed on an unsupported file as a fail with legal exposure, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every for-cause code is supported by dated evidence, matches the state definition and shows pre-transmission counsel review.

testing.step: Test producer notice issuance and delivery
actions: Pull the producer notice letter for each sampled termination and read its date against the state filing date.
Recompute the notice due date from the state's producer-notice window and record days early or late.
Confirm the letter went to the address of record on the PDB and that delivery proof is attached.
Flag notices that omit a reason the state requires the producer to receive.
testing.done: every sampled termination shows a dated producer notice, a recomputed due date and attached delivery proof.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per late or missing filing with state, NPN, trigger date, filing date, days over and premium written in the gap.
Assign a root cause — trigger not detected, wrong window in the table, rejection not reworked, termination not cascaded to every state — and an owner.
Record the state's response to any late filing, including fees assessed or reinstatement required.
Carry every open item into the next quarter as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every timeliness exception has an issue, day count, root cause, owner, remediation date and recorded state consequence.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute on-time filing rates separately for appointments and terminations, by state, and compare to the 100% threshold.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer, who submitted none of the sampled transactions, sign the workpaper.
Report the state-level late-filing profile to the Compliance Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states on-time rates by state, the conclusion and the committee reporting date, filed in the repository.

checklist.step: Build the renewal calendar from the licence inventory
actions: Extract every active licence the company depends on: resident and non-resident producer licences by NPN and state, business entity licences by FEIN, appointment renewals, and the company certificates of authority from the authority register.
Populate the renewal log with expiry or continuation date, renewal cycle length, renewing authority and the fee amount for each row.
Flag rows where the expiry date is missing or is more than one cycle in the past — those are almost always already-lapsed licences.
Sort the log by expiry date and publish the next 180 days as the working calendar.
checklist.done: the renewal log holds every licence the company relies on, with an expiry date, cycle and fee, and a published 180-day calendar.

checklist.step: Confirm each state's renewal cycle and expiry convention
actions: For each state read the DOI licensing page for the cycle: annual or biennial, and whether expiry falls on the licensee's birth month end, the licence anniversary or a fixed statewide date.
Record whether non-resident licences follow the resident state's cycle or the non-resident state's own cycle, because the two conventions produce different dates.
Record for business entity licences whether the cycle differs from individual licences in that state.
Date and initial each state entry and re-validate any entry older than 12 months before relying on it.
checklist.done: each state entry names the cycle, expiry convention and non-resident treatment, with a validation date.

checklist.step: Pull the state CE requirement for each cycle
actions: For each state record total CE hours required per cycle, the ethics-hour subset, any line-specific requirement (annuity suitability, long-term care, flood, or state-specific law hours) and the carry-forward rule.
Record which producers are exempt — commonly by years licensed or by designation — and the evidence the state accepts for the exemption.
Record the state's CE administrator and the reporting lag between course completion and the transcript updating.
Publish the requirement table to Learning & Development so course catalogues are built against real state rules.
checklist.done: a per-state CE table exists with total hours, ethics hours, line-specific hours, exemptions and reporting lag.

checklist.step: Monitor CE transcripts against the requirement at T-120
actions: At 120 days before each expiry, pull the PDB and the state CE transcript for the NPN and read completed hours by category.
Subtract completed from required to produce a per-producer hours gap, separating general hours from ethics and line-specific hours.
Publish the gap list to the Agency Relations Manager and the producer, naming the exact hours outstanding and the state deadline.
Record the gap and the notification date on the renewal log row.
checklist.done: every licence expiring in 120 days has a categorised CE gap figure and a dated notification to the producer.

checklist.step: Close CE gaps through the learning management system and approved providers
actions: Assign state-approved courses covering the outstanding general, ethics and line-specific hours, checking each course carries the state's CE provider and course approval number.
Set the completion due date at least 15 business days before the state deadline to absorb the CE reporting lag.
Collect completion certificates showing provider number, course number, hours and completion date, and file them against the producer record.
Report weekly completion progress against the gap list to the Producer Licensing Coordinator.
checklist.done: assigned courses cover every outstanding hour category, and completion certificates with approval numbers are on file.

checklist.step: Verify the CE hours have actually posted to the state transcript
actions: At T-30 re-pull the state CE transcript and confirm the completed hours appear against the licence, not just in the internal learning record.
Chase the provider directly where hours completed more than the reporting lag ago have not posted, quoting the course approval number and completion date.
Escalate unposted hours to the Producer Compliance Manager at T-15 because renewal will be refused on a short transcript.
Record the confirmed posted hours on the renewal log row.
checklist.done: the state transcript itself shows sufficient hours for every licence renewing within 30 days, or the shortfall is escalated.

checklist.step: Submit the producer licence renewal and fee
actions: In NIPR Gateway open the renewal transaction for the state and NPN, confirm the lines being renewed and answer the state's background questions.
Pay the state renewal fee and any NIPR transaction fee and capture the confirmation number and timestamp.
Where the state does not accept renewal through NIPR, submit through the state's own portal and capture that confirmation instead.
Write the confirmation number, payment date and renewal channel onto the renewal log row.
checklist.done: each renewal is submitted and paid with a captured confirmation number, timestamp and channel on the log row.

checklist.step: Renew business entity licences and appointment renewals
actions: Renew each agency entity licence by FEIN and confirm the designated responsible licensee named on the renewal still holds an active individual licence.
Pay the states that bill appointment renewals on an annual or biennial invoice, matching each invoice line to an appointment on the register before payment.
Query any invoice line for a producer already terminated — paying it re-affirms an appointment that should be closed.
Record every entity and appointment renewal confirmation against the register.
checklist.done: entity licences and appointment renewals are paid against reconciled invoice lines with confirmations recorded.

checklist.step: Continue the company certificate of authority on its state cycle
actions: For each state's continuation date confirm the annual statement and any state continuation form were filed and the fee paid, commonly through NAIC OPTins.
Confirm capital, surplus and the statutory deposit still meet the state's minimum using the most recently filed Annual Statement figures.
Record the continuation confirmation against the authority register row and roll the continuation date forward.
Escalate immediately any state that has not acknowledged continuation within 10 business days of its renewal date.
checklist.done: every certificate shows a paid, acknowledged continuation with capital and deposit conditions re-tested.

checklist.step: Confirm the renewal landed and the licence reads active
actions: Re-pull the PDB 5 business days after each renewal submission and read the status, the new expiry date and the lines carried forward.
Compare the renewed lines to the pre-renewal lines — a line silently dropped at renewal will surface later as unlicensed activity.
Update the renewal log with the new expiry date and set the next cycle's alerts.
Close the row only when the PDB shows Active with the new expiry.
checklist.done: each renewal is confirmed active on the PDB with the new expiry date and an unchanged line set recorded.

checklist.step: Handle expirations and lapses without letting business continue
actions: On any expiry without a confirmed renewal, set the producer to solicit-blocked and suspend portal entitlements for that state the same day.
Determine whether the state offers a reinstatement window with a late fee or requires a fresh licence application with re-examination.
Pull the business written between expiry and block, quantify premium and commission with the Commission Analyst, and route to Compliance for exception logging.
Record the reinstatement path chosen, its cost and its completion date.
checklist.done: every lapse is blocked the same day, the gap business is quantified, and a reinstatement path is chosen and dated.

checklist.step: Escalate systemic renewal risk to distribution leadership
actions: Publish monthly the count of licences expiring in 30/60/90 days, the count with an open CE gap and the lapse count for the month.
Break the CE gap figures out by agency so persistently non-compliant agencies are visible to the Head of Distribution.
Table the report at distribution governance with a recommendation for agencies whose producers repeatedly reach T-30 with open gaps.
Record decisions and owners against the renewal log.
checklist.done: a monthly expiry, CE-gap and lapse report is tabled at distribution governance with agency-level breakout and recorded decisions.

checklist.step: Re-validate the state cycle and CE table each January
actions: Re-read each state's licensing and CE pages and compare hours, ethics subset, line-specific requirements and cycle conventions to the internal table.
Record every change with its effective date and identify which producers are affected mid-cycle.
Re-issue the requirement table to Learning & Development and re-baseline any open CE gap figures affected by a change.
Have the Producer Compliance Manager approve the revised table before it drives renewal alerts.
checklist.done: the state cycle and CE table is re-validated, changes are dated, affected producers identified and the table re-approved.

checklist.step: Reconcile renewal fee spend to the licences actually renewed
actions: Pull the month's NIPR fee statement and any state renewal invoices and match each charge to a renewal log row on NPN, state and confirmation number.
Compare each amount paid to the state's published renewal fee and query under- or overpayments with the state, since an underpaid renewal is not a completed renewal.
List charges with no matching renewal row and renewal rows with no charge, and clear both before the month closes.
Hand the reconciliation and the unresolved list to the Producer Compliance Manager with the month-end sign-off.
checklist.done: every renewal charge matches a log row at the published fee and unmatched items are cleared before month close.

checklist.step: Retain renewal and CE evidence
actions: File renewal confirmations, fee receipts, CE transcripts and course completion certificates under Licensing / Renewals / <state> / <NPN>.
Apply the 5-years-from-cycle-end retention label on CE evidence and the 7-years-after-termination label on renewal confirmations.
Confirm records are retrievable by NPN, state, expiry date and CE cycle.
Link the repository record back to the renewal log row.
checklist.done: renewal and CE evidence is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by NPN, state and cycle.

testing.step: Build the population of licences expiring or continuing in the quarter
actions: Extract every producer, entity and company licence with an expiry or continuation date inside the quarter, with state, NPN or FEIN, lines and cycle length.
Add every CE cycle ending in the quarter with the required and completed hours as recorded internally.
Reconcile the expiry list to a fresh PDB extract of the active roster so licences missing from the internal log are exposed.
Sign and date the population as complete.
testing.done: the expiry and CE population reconciles to a PDB roster extract and is signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the renewal log and to regulator records
actions: Match every expiring licence to a renewal log row with a confirmation number and payment date.
Pull the current PDB status for each and confirm it reads Active with an expiry date one cycle forward.
List licences with no renewal row, no confirmation number or a still-past expiry as automatic exceptions.
Separately list licences that renewed with fewer lines than before as scope-loss exceptions.
testing.done: every expiring licence matches a confirmed renewal with a forward expiry on the PDB, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of company certificate continuations and 100% of licences that lapsed at any point in the quarter.
Take 30 producer licences by seeded random selection stratified across resident and non-resident licences.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date for reproducibility.
State the number of distinct jurisdictions represented.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, covers all continuations and lapses, and its jurisdiction coverage is stated.

testing.step: Re-verify renewal status directly at the regulator
actions: Pull a fresh PDB for each sampled NPN and, for company certificates, the state DOI company lookup, without reading the internal record first.
Record status, expiry or continuation date and lines from your own retrieval.
Compare to the renewal log and treat any difference as an exception, including an internal expiry date more generous than the regulator's.
Capture the retrieved screens with dates into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled licence has an independently retrieved regulator record compared to the renewal log.

testing.step: Recompute the CE requirement and re-read the transcript
actions: Read the state's own CE rule for the sampled licence and record required total hours, ethics hours and any line-specific hours for that cycle.
Read the state CE transcript and total the posted hours by category as at the cycle end date, not today.
Compare to the internal CE record and flag any cycle that closed short, including cycles where an exemption was claimed without the evidence the state accepts.
Record the recomputation and the rule source for each sampled licence.
testing.done: CE hours are recomputed from the state rule and transcript for every sampled licence, with exemptions evidenced.

testing.step: Trace renewal payments to receipts and reconcile fees
actions: Match each sampled renewal confirmation number to a NIPR fee statement line or a state receipt for the correct fee amount.
Compare the fee paid to the state's published renewal fee and flag under- or overpayments, since underpayment leaves a renewal incomplete.
Confirm appointment renewal invoice lines paid in the quarter correspond to appointments that were still active.
Record the reconciliation and the unmatched items in the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled renewal traces to a receipt at the published fee, and appointment renewal payments reconcile to active appointments.

testing.step: Recompute the alert timing and test that reminders fired
actions: For each sampled licence recompute the T-120/T-90/T-60/T-30/T-10 alert dates from the confirmed expiry date.
Pull the notification history and confirm each alert actually issued to a named recipient on or before the computed date.
Flag licences renewed inside 10 days of expiry as a control weakness even where no lapse occurred.
Record alert-fire evidence and the days-to-expiry at renewal for each sampled row.
testing.done: alert dates are recomputed and matched to issued notifications, with days-to-expiry at renewal recorded.

testing.step: Test business written during any lapse period
actions: For every lapsed licence in the quarter, extract policies bound and applications taken between the expiry date and the reinstatement or block date.
Quantify premium and commission on that business and confirm commissions were placed in withholding.
Confirm portal entitlements were suspended on the expiry date rather than on the day the lapse was noticed.
Any business written during a lapse is a reportable breach, not a test exception.
testing.done: lapse-period business is extracted and quantified for every lapse, with entitlement suspension timing evidenced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per lapse, short CE cycle, missed continuation or scope-loss renewal with state, NPN, dates and premium at risk.
Assign a root cause — licence absent from the log, wrong cycle convention, CE hours not posted in time, fee underpaid — and an owner.
Record the reinstatement path, cost and completion date for each lapse, and Regulatory Counsel's view where business was written.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, for lapses, a documented reinstatement outcome.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the on-time renewal rate, the lapse count and the CE shortfall count and compare to the zero-lapse threshold.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer, who processed none of the sampled renewals, sign the workpaper.
Report lapses and any lapse-period writing to the Compliance Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states renewal rates, lapse counts, the conclusion and the committee reporting date, filed in the repository.

Code § 1668, Connecticut Gen. Stat. § 38a-774
