Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every employee hired or transferred into an insurance function in the quarter, every producer and agency contracted in the quarter, and every conviction disclosed during the quarter by an existing worker or producer

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — one person performing insurance work without a completed screening, or one prohibited person engaged without a valid written consent, is a fail and is reported to the Head of Compliance the same day

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is per hire and per contracting event, so the test runs quarterly over that quarter's hires and contractings, with 100% coverage of any adjudicated felony case

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have adjudicated or approved any sampled screening decision

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly 1033 screening test workpaper (hire and contracting population, screening dates, adjudication re-performance, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under Licensing / 1033 Screening, restricted access

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Screening register by person with screening date, result, adjudication decision and consent letter reference, redacted for sensitive personal data, producible to a DOI examiner within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Compliance Manager responds to DOI inquiries about a named individual; Employment Counsel and Regulatory Counsel jointly clear any response confirming that a prohibited person performed insurance work

checklist.step: Decide whether the role is in scope for 1033 screening
actions: Read the job description or the producer contract and decide whether the person will be engaged in the business of insurance — underwriting, claims, sales, premium handling, policy service, actuarial, or supervision of those functions.
Include contractors, temporary staff and third-party administrator personnel who touch those functions, because § 1033 follows the activity, not the payroll.
Record the in-scope decision, the reasoning and the reviewer on the requisition or contracting record; a role marked out of scope must state why.
Publish the in-scope role list to the Recruiter Talent Acquisition Specialist so screening is triggered automatically at offer.
checklist.done: the requisition or contracting record carries a dated in-scope decision with reasoning, and the recruiter has the trigger list.

checklist.step: Obtain the signed screening authorisation and disclosure
actions: Issue the FCRA standalone disclosure and the written authorisation for a consumer report, keeping the disclosure on its own document with no extraneous waiver text.
Issue any state-specific notice the candidate's work location requires, including summary-of-rights documents.
Collect the signed authorisation and full legal name, prior names, date of birth and address history needed for an accurate search.
Attach the signed set to the candidate record and record the authorisation date.
checklist.done: a compliant standalone disclosure and signed authorisation with full identity history are on the candidate record.

checklist.step: Order the background package matched to the role
actions: Order the package for in-scope roles: county criminal for every county of residence in the last 7–10 years, statewide and federal criminal, national criminal database, sex offender registry, and identity/SSN trace.
Add OFAC and sanctions screening, and for roles handling money add a credit check where the jurisdiction allows it.
Confirm the SSN trace address history matches the candidate's declared history, and order additional county searches for any address the trace surfaces that the candidate did not declare.
Record the order date, the vendor reference and the searches ordered on the candidate record.
checklist.done: the ordered package covers every jurisdiction in the trace-verified address history, with the vendor reference recorded.

checklist.step: Adjudicate any criminal record against the 1033 test
actions: For each reported offence record the charge, the jurisdiction, the statute, the disposition, the conviction date and whether it was a felony.

Apply the § 1033(e)(1) test: is it a criminal felony involving dishonesty or a breach of trust, or a violation of § 1033 itself — theft, fraud, embezzlement, forgery, false statements and misappropriation being the core set.
Where the disposition is a deferred adjudication, expungement or pardon, obtain the court record rather than relying on the vendor summary, because the effect on the prohibition differs by outcome.
Record a written determination — prohibited, not prohibited, or unresolved pending records — with the reasoning and the reviewer name and date.
checklist.done: every reported offence has a written prohibited/not-prohibited determination citing the felony and dishonesty/breach-of-trust test.

checklist.step: Get Employment Counsel review on every prohibited determination
actions: Review the court record, the determination and the role-in-scope decision for each case adjudicated as prohibited.
Confirm the adjudication also complies with fair-chance and ban-the-box rules in the work jurisdiction, including any individualised assessment requirement.
Confirm or overturn the determination in writing on the case record, with the date.
Advise whether the person may be considered for an out-of-scope role instead of a refusal.
checklist.done: every prohibited determination carries a dated counsel confirmation and a fair-chance compliance note.

checklist.step: Verify any claimed 1033 written consent from the state regulator
actions: Where the individual produces a § 1033(e)(2) written consent, read the letter for the issuing state, the individual's name, the offence covered, the effective date and any conditions or expiry.
Confirm the letter directly with the issuing DOI's licensing division and record the contact, date and confirmation method — a photocopy alone is not evidence.
Check the consent's scope covers the state or states the person will work in and the activity they will perform; a consent from one state does not automatically travel.
File the verified letter under restricted access and record its conditions and any expiry on the person's record.
checklist.done: each consent letter is verified with the issuing DOI and its scope, conditions and expiry are recorded on the person's record.

checklist.step: Run the FCRA adverse action sequence where a report drives the decision
actions: Send the pre-adverse action notice with a copy of the consumer report and the summary of rights, and record the send date.
Hold the decision open for the waiting period — at least 5 business days as the working standard — so the candidate can dispute inaccuracies.
Log any dispute and route it to the vendor for re-investigation, pausing the decision until the corrected report returns.
Send the final adverse action notice naming the consumer reporting agency and stating it did not make the decision, and file both notices.
checklist.done: pre-adverse and final adverse notices are dated, separated by the waiting period, with any dispute resolved before the final notice.

checklist.step: Hold the engagement gate until screening clears
actions: Keep the worker record in a pre-hire state that does not provision system access until the screening status reads Cleared.
Coordinate with the Identity Access Manager so policy admin, claims and underwriting entitlements are not granted against an uncleared record.
Where a start date must move, notify the hiring manager in writing rather than allowing a conditional start into insurance work.
Record the clearance date and the first day of insurance work so the two can be compared later.
checklist.done: no in-scope worker has system access or performs insurance work before a recorded clearance date.

checklist.step: Apply the same gate to producers and agency staff
actions: For each contracting producer, read the PDB regulatory actions and the background report together, because a state action can flag conduct the criminal search will not.
Require the agency to attest in the agency contract that its sub-producers and staff engaged in the business of insurance have been screened, and require notification of any conviction.
Adjudicate producer criminal records on the same § 1033 test and record the determination on the producer record.
Keep the producer at 'Pending — unverified' until the determination is recorded, so no portal entitlement can be released.
checklist.done: every contracting producer and attesting agency has a recorded § 1033 determination before entitlements are released.

checklist.step: Capture conviction disclosures from existing staff and producers
actions: Maintain the standing obligation in the code of conduct and the producer agreement to report any felony charge or conviction within 5 business days.
Re-affirm the obligation in the annual compliance attestation so silence becomes an attested fact rather than an omission.
On any disclosure, open a screening case the same day, obtain the court record and adjudicate on the § 1033 test.
Suspend the person from insurance functions while the case is open where the disclosed offence is on its face a dishonesty felony.
checklist.done: disclosures are captured within 5 business days, adjudicated on court records, and high-risk cases are suspended pending outcome.

checklist.step: Support a consent application where the business wants to retain the person
actions: Decide with the Head of Compliance whether to sponsor a § 1033(e)(2) written consent application to the state insurance regulator.
Assemble the application to the state's published form: individual's statement, court records, disposition documents, rehabilitation evidence, proposed role and supervision plan.
Submit to the DOI licensing division and log the submission date, the reviewer and any conditions the state signals.
Keep the individual out of insurance functions until the written consent is in hand — a pending application is not a consent.
checklist.done: consent applications are filed with full court records and the individual stays out of insurance work until the consent issues.

checklist.step: Re-screen on the defined cycle and on trigger events
actions: Re-screen in-scope employees on the cycle the procedure sets and on promotion into a money-handling or supervisory insurance role.
Re-screen producers at each contract renewal and on any new PDB regulatory action alert.
Run continuous criminal monitoring where the vendor offers it, and treat each alert as a new screening case.
Record the re-screen date and result on the person's record so the currency of the clearance is always visible.
checklist.done: each in-scope person shows a current clearance date driven by the cycle and by triggers, with alerts worked as cases.

checklist.step: Restrict access to screening data
actions: Limit the screening evidence folder to a named need-to-know list of Compliance, HR and Legal roles and review that list quarterly.
Confirm background reports are not copied into general HR files, hiring manager mailboxes or the producer record visible to distribution staff.
Enable access logging on the folder and review the log for out-of-pattern reads.
Record the quarterly access review with the reviewer and date.
checklist.done: screening evidence is restricted to a reviewed need-to-know list with access logging and a dated quarterly review.

checklist.step: Report screening outcomes into compliance governance
actions: Report quarterly the count of in-scope screenings completed, prohibited determinations, consents verified, consent applications filed and open cases.
Report any instance of insurance work performed before clearance with the dates and functions involved.
Table the report at the Compliance Committee with recommendations where a channel or agency shows repeated failures.
Record decisions, owners and dates against the screening case log.
checklist.done: a quarterly screening report including any pre-clearance work is tabled at the Compliance Committee with recorded decisions.

checklist.step: Retain screening evidence under restricted access
actions: File authorisations, reports, adjudications, counsel reviews, consent letters and adverse action notices under Licensing / 1033 Screening / <person id>.
Apply the 7-years-after-engagement-end retention label and the restricted-access classification.
Confirm the record is retrievable by person id and screening date without exposing the underlying report to general search.
Link the record to the HRIS worker record or the producer record without copying the report content into either.
checklist.done: screening evidence is filed, restricted, retention-labelled and retrievable by person id and screening date.

testing.step: Build the population of in-scope hires, contractings and disclosures
actions: Extract every hire, rehire and internal transfer into an insurance function in the quarter with start date, role, work state and requisition id.
Extract every producer and agency contracted in the quarter from the producer management system with contract execution date.
Extract every conviction disclosure logged in the quarter from the compliance case log.
Reconcile the hire extract to payroll new-starter records so contractors and temporary staff cannot be omitted, and sign the population.
testing.done: hire, contracting and disclosure populations reconcile to payroll and producer records and are signed as complete.

testing.step: Reconcile each in-scope person to a completed screening
actions: Match each population row to a screening record with an authorisation date, a vendor report date and an adjudication decision.
Compare the clearance date to the first day of insurance work or the entitlement release date.
List rows with no screening, no adjudication or a clearance date after work started as automatic exceptions.
Test the in-scope determination for a sample of roles marked out of scope, because a wrong scoping decision hides the whole control.
testing.done: every in-scope person matches a completed screening cleared before work started, or is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample
actions: Take 100% of cases with any reported criminal record, 100% of prohibited determinations and 100% of verified consent letters.
Take 25 clean screenings by seeded random selection across employees and producers.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date for reproducibility.
Note the work jurisdictions represented so fair-chance overlays can be tested where they apply.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and includes every record-bearing case, prohibited determination and consent letter.

testing.step: Re-perform the 1033 adjudication on the record-bearing cases
actions: Read the court disposition record for each sampled offence and independently classify felony versus misdemeanour and dishonesty/breach-of-trust versus not.
Reach your own § 1033(e)(1) conclusion before reading the filed determination.
Compare and treat any difference as an exception, including a correct conclusion supported by the wrong reasoning.
Record the re-performance and the court record reference for each sampled case.
testing.done: each record-bearing case has an independent re-performed § 1033 conclusion tied to a court record reference.

testing.step: Verify consent letters independently with the issuing regulator
actions: For each sampled consent letter, contact the issuing DOI licensing division and confirm the letter, its date, its scope and any conditions.
Compare the confirmed scope to the states and activities the person actually performs, taken from the HRIS role or the producer appointment list.
Flag any person working in a state or activity the consent does not cover, and any consent past a condition or expiry date.
Record the regulator contact, date and method in the workpaper.
testing.done: each consent letter is confirmed with the issuing regulator and its scope compared to the person's actual activity.

testing.step: Test screening package completeness against the address history
actions: Compare the SSN trace address history on the vendor report to the counties actually searched for each sampled case.
Flag any county of residence in the look-back period with no corresponding county criminal search — an unsearched county is an untested jurisdiction.
Confirm federal criminal and sanctions searches were included for every in-scope role.
Record the gap analysis per sampled case.
testing.done: every sampled screening shows county searches covering the traced address history plus federal and sanctions searches.

testing.step: Test the FCRA adverse action sequence and timing
actions: For each sampled adverse decision read the pre-adverse notice, the report copy and the summary of rights and record the send date.
Recompute the waiting period to the final adverse action notice and flag any decision made inside it.
Confirm the disclosure was a standalone document and the authorisation was signed before the report was ordered.
Flag jurisdictions requiring an individualised assessment where none is documented.
testing.done: every sampled adverse decision shows a compliant disclosure, a recomputed waiting period and any required individualised assessment.

testing.step: Test access restrictions on screening evidence
actions: Extract the access list for the screening evidence folder and compare it to the approved need-to-know list.
Read the access log for the quarter and identify reads by anyone outside that list or outside a live case.
Search general HR and producer folders for copies of background reports that should not have left the restricted area.
Record every unapproved access and every stray copy with its owner.
testing.done: the folder access list matches the approved need-to-know list and every unapproved read or stray copy is identified.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with the person id, role, dates worked, functions performed and the control that failed.
Assign a root cause — role wrongly scoped out, start date beat the screening, county gap in the package, consent not verified — and an owner.
For any prohibited person who performed insurance work, record the removal date and Employment Counsel's decision on regulator notification.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, for prohibited-person work, a removal date and counsel decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate over in-scope hires and contractings and compare it to the zero-tolerance threshold.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer, who adjudicated none of the sampled screenings, sign the workpaper.
Report results and any prohibited-person engagement to the Compliance Committee and file the signed, access-restricted workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed, restricted workpaper states the exception rate, conclusion and committee reporting date and is filed in the repository.

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly roster reconciliation test workpaper (three extracts, match output, break register, re-performed matching, exceptions) in the compliance evidence repository under Licensing / Roster Reconciliation

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Reconciliation summary by state showing roster count, state appointment count, transacting count, breaks by category and corrective transactions, producible in a market conduct licensing data call within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Producer Compliance Manager answers DOI appointment data calls; Regulatory Counsel clears any response disclosing business written without an appointment of record

checklist.step: Open the quarterly reconciliation and fix the as-of date
actions: Set the as-of date to the last calendar day of the quarter and state it on the reconciliation cover sheet so all three extracts describe the same instant.
Confirm with the Distribution Operations Manager that no roster maintenance backlog straddles the date, and list any known in-flight transactions.
Name the preparer, the reviewer and the target clearance date on the cover sheet.
Open the break register for the quarter with categories pre-defined so breaks cannot be recorded as free text.
checklist.done: the cover sheet fixes the as-of date, names preparer and reviewer, and an empty categorised break register is open.

checklist.step: Extract the internal producer roster
actions: Extract every producer-state-company row with NPN, producer legal name, FEIN for entities, writing company NAIC code, status, eligibility date and termination date.
Include rows terminated during the quarter, because a terminated producer with a live state appointment is exactly the break being hunted.
Check every row carries an NPN and a company NAIC code; rows missing either cannot be matched and must be repaired before the run.
Record the extract row count, timestamp and the query used on the cover sheet.
checklist.done: the roster extract is keyed on NPN + state + NAIC code with no missing keys, and its count and timestamp are recorded.

checklist.step: Pull the state appointment file from NIPR
actions: In NIPR Gateway request the appointment reconciliation file for each writing company NAIC code covering all appointing states.
Read each row's NPN, state, appointment status, appointment effective date and appointment type or line.
Confirm the file covers every state the company is authorised in — a missing state in the file will read as zero appointments and hide breaks.
Record the file date, row count and the NAIC codes requested on the cover sheet.
checklist.done: a dated NIPR appointment file covering every authorised state is loaded with its row count recorded.

checklist.step: Extract the producers who actually transacted in the quarter
actions: Extract distinct writing producer NPN by risk state and writing company for every new business and renewal transaction bound in the quarter.
Extract from the commission platform every producer paid commission in the quarter by state, since commission paid without an appointment is a separate exposure.
Union the two into one transacting population and note which source contributed each row.
Record counts and timestamps on the cover sheet.
checklist.done: a transacting population exists from both policy and commission sources with row counts and source flags recorded.

checklist.step: Run the three-way match on NPN, state and company code
actions: Match roster to NIPR to transacting on the composite key NPN + state + NAIC company code.
Produce four outputs: matched all three, roster-only, state-only, transacting-only, plus roster-and-state-but-not-transacting.
Verify the four output counts sum back to the input populations before any interpretation begins.
Save the match workbook with the formulas intact so the run can be reproduced.
checklist.done: the match runs on the composite key, the outputs reconcile back to the input counts, and the workbook is saved reproducible.

checklist.step: Categorise every break
actions: Assign each break a category: TRANSACTING-NOT-APPOINTED, APPOINTED-NOT-ON-ROSTER, ROSTER-NOT-APPOINTED, TERMINATED-BUT-STILL-APPOINTED, DUPLICATE NPN, or DATA-KEY-ERROR.
Rank TRANSACTING-NOT-APPOINTED first — that is business written without an appointment of record and it carries the direct regulatory exposure.
Assign each break an owner and a clearance due date inside the 20-business-day window.
Write the counts by category and by state onto the reconciliation summary.
checklist.done: every break has a category, an owner and a due date, and the summary shows counts by category and by state.

checklist.step: Clear transacting-not-appointed breaks first
actions: For each break identify the earliest transaction date in the state and treat it as the statutory trigger date.
Re-pull the PDB to confirm the producer holds an active licence with the required line, and stop if it does not.
File the appointment in NIPR immediately and capture the transaction id, then compute the days between the trigger date and the filing date.
Where the filing is outside the state window, hand the break to Compliance as a late-filing exception with the day count and the premium written in the gap.
checklist.done: every transacting-not-appointed break has an appointment filed, a day count against the state window and a premium figure.

checklist.step: Clear appointed-not-on-roster and terminated-but-still-appointed breaks
actions: Establish whether the producer relationship genuinely ended by reading the contract file and asking the Agency Relations Manager.
Where it ended, file the termination in NIPR using the correct state reason code and the actual termination effective date, not the reconciliation date.
Where the relationship is live but the roster row is missing, repair the roster rather than terminating a valid appointment.
Record the corrective transaction id and the state acknowledgement against the break.
checklist.done: each such break ends in either a filed termination with the true effective date or a repaired roster row, with evidence attached.

checklist.step: Clear roster-not-appointed breaks
actions: Check whether the state is appointment-optional or notification-only, in which case no appointment is expected and the row is explained rather than corrected.
Where an appointment is required and the producer is expected to write, file it and confirm the producer's licence supports the lines.
Where the producer will not write in that state, remove the state from the roster row so the roster stops overstating reach.
Record the disposition and the reasoning on the break.
checklist.done: each roster-not-appointed break is filed, explained by state rule, or removed from the roster with reasoning recorded.

checklist.step: Resolve duplicate NPN and data-key errors at source
actions: Identify duplicate producer records sharing an NPN and merge them to a single golden record with the correct legal name and TIN.
Repair rows with missing or malformed NPNs and NAIC codes by re-verifying against the PDB rather than guessing.
Add a validation rule that blocks creation of a producer record without a PDB-verified NPN.
Record the merged and repaired record ids on the break so the fix is auditable.
checklist.done: duplicate and malformed producer keys are merged or repaired against the PDB and a creation-time validation rule is in place.

checklist.step: Review the fee and commission consequences of the breaks
actions: Total commission paid in the quarter to producers in any TRANSACTING-NOT-APPOINTED or terminated-but-paid break.
Place disputed commission into withholding pending the disposition and notify the Agency Relations Manager.
Identify appointment fees paid for producers with no roster row, since those are avoidable state fees on appointments that should be closed.
Report both figures on the reconciliation summary.
checklist.done: commission at risk and avoidable appointment fees are quantified and disputed commission is placed in withholding.

checklist.step: Age and escalate unresolved breaks
actions: Age every open break from the reconciliation as-of date and report the ageing weekly to the Producer Compliance Manager.
Escalate any break aged past 30 days to the Head of Compliance with the reason it remains open and the exposure attached.
Raise a tracker issue for every break that involved business written without an appointment, with root cause and owner.
Carry unresolved breaks into the next quarter's reconciliation as opening items rather than closing them silently.
checklist.done: breaks are aged weekly, items past 30 days are escalated, and unresolved breaks are carried forward as opening items.

checklist.step: Sign off the reconciliation and report it
actions: Review the reconciliation summary: three population counts, break counts by category and state, clearance status and residual exposure.
Confirm every TRANSACTING-NOT-APPOINTED break has a filed appointment and a quantified gap before signing.
Sign and date the reconciliation and report the results to the Compliance Committee with the top root causes.
Record committee decisions and owners against the reconciliation cover sheet.
checklist.done: the reconciliation is signed and dated with all transacting breaks filed and quantified, and reported to the committee.

checklist.step: Feed root causes back into the operating process
actions: Group the quarter's breaks by root cause — trigger not detected, termination not cascaded to every state, roster key errors, appointment-optional states misconfigured.
Agree one process or system change per recurring cause with the Distribution Operations Manager and set an owner and date.
Where the cause is a system gate, raise the change with the Policy Admin Ops Lead so the block happens at quote rather than at reconciliation.
Track the agreed changes to completion and re-measure the same cause next quarter.
checklist.done: each recurring root cause has an owned, dated process or system change tracked to completion and re-measured next quarter.

checklist.step: Retain the reconciliation evidence
actions: File the cover sheet, three extracts, match workbook, break register, corrective transaction confirmations and the signed summary under Licensing / Roster Reconciliation / <quarter>.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the reconciliation date.
Confirm the record is retrievable by quarter, state and NPN.
Link the reconciliation to the appointment register so a break can be traced to its corrective transaction in one hop.
checklist.done: the full reconciliation package is filed, retention-labelled and retrievable by quarter, state and NPN.

testing.step: Re-extract the three populations independently
actions: Re-run the roster extract at the same as-of date using your own query and compare the row count to the preparer's.
Request your own NIPR appointment reconciliation file for the same NAIC codes and states and compare its row count to the file used.
Re-extract distinct transacting producer-state rows from policy admin and commissions for the quarter.
Investigate and document any count difference before relying on the preparer's populations.
testing.done: three independently re-extracted populations exist with every count difference against the preparer's investigated and explained.

testing.step: Reconcile the preparer's match output back to the populations
actions: Add the preparer's matched and break categories and confirm the total equals the input population counts with no rows dropped.
Check the match key used was NPN + state + NAIC company code, and re-run a sample of matches on your own extracts.
Flag any silent exclusion — inactive statuses filtered out, states omitted, or a company code left out of the NIPR request.
Document the reconciliation of counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: the match output reconciles row for row to the populations and any silent exclusion is identified.

testing.step: Draw and document the sample of breaks
actions: Take 100% of TRANSACTING-NOT-APPOINTED breaks and 100% of breaks aged over 30 days.
Take 25 further breaks by seeded random selection across the remaining categories.
Record the seed, population size, stratification and selection date for reproducibility.
State how many states and how many writing companies the sample touches.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible, includes every transacting break and aged break, and its state and company coverage is stated.

testing.step: Re-perform the break categorisation
actions: For each sampled break read the underlying roster row, NIPR row and transaction record and assign your own category before reading the preparer's.
Compare and treat any recategorisation as an exception, especially a transacting break recorded as a data-key error.
Check that appointment-optional state claims are supported by the state's own rule text, not by convention.
Record the re-performed category and the evidence relied on for each sampled break.
testing.done: each sampled break has an independently assigned category compared to the preparer's, with state-rule support where claimed.

testing.step: Trace corrective transactions to NIPR confirmations
actions: Look up each recorded corrective appointment or termination transaction id in NIPR Gateway and confirm it exists for the right company, state and NPN.
Read the state's returned status and effective date and compare to the break register.
For terminations, confirm the effective date is the true relationship end date rather than the reconciliation date.
Capture the transaction detail screens into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled corrective transaction traces to a confirmed NIPR record with the correct effective date captured.

testing.step: Recompute the statutory day count on late-cured breaks
actions: For each sampled transacting break, take the earliest transaction date in the state as the trigger and read the state's statutory window from the statute.
Recompute days from trigger to actual appointment filing and compare to the preparer's figure.
Recompute the premium written between the trigger date and the appointment effective date from the policy extract.
Flag any break where the preparer's day count or premium figure understates the exposure.
testing.done: day counts and gap premium are independently recomputed for every sampled transacting break and compared to the preparer's.

testing.step: Test the completeness of the transacting population
actions: Reconcile the transacting population to total commission paid in the quarter and to bound premium by state.
Identify producers paid commission who do not appear in the transacting extract, since split or house accounts often hide there.
Confirm sub-producers writing under an agency appear individually where the state appoints individuals rather than firms.
Document the completeness testing and any producers added to the population.
testing.done: the transacting population reconciles to commission and premium totals and every omitted producer is identified.

testing.step: Test break ageing and escalation discipline
actions: Recompute ageing on every open break from the as-of date and compare to the register's reported ageing.
Confirm breaks past 30 days were escalated to the Head of Compliance with a documented reason and exposure.
Confirm breaks carried forward from the prior quarter appear as opening items and were not silently closed.
Record ageing accuracy and any escalation that did not happen.
testing.done: ageing is recomputed, escalations past 30 days are evidenced, and prior-quarter carry-forwards are traced.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise an issue per exception with state, NPN, break category, day count, premium and the control that failed.
Assign a root cause — population incomplete, wrong match key, break miscategorised, corrective transaction not filed — and an owner.
For business written without an appointment, record Regulatory Counsel's view on state notification and on commission treatment.
Carry every open item into the next quarter as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue, root cause, owner, remediation date and, where business was unappointed, a counsel view on notification.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the break rate by category and by state and compare it to the zero-unexplained-break threshold.
State the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with workpaper references.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared no part of the reconciliation and cleared no sampled break, sign the workpaper.
Report break rates, unappointed writing and root causes to the Compliance Committee and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states break rates by category and state, the conclusion and the committee reporting date, filed in the repository.
